law.what: One pinned upper bound per program per kernel envelope, priced in the kernel's own verifier cost: the verified_insns count bpf_prog_info reports for the loaded program (UAPI aba64c7da983 - bpf: Add verified_insns to bpf_prog_info and fdinfo), read live by the census in scripts/supermassive/verifier-budget-test.py through the staged bpftool. The objects are byte-identical by construction (the parity gates), so for one kernel the number is deterministic - the budget pins the verifier walk, not a sample of it.
law.growth_law: A measured value above the pinned budget fails the battery. Raising a budget requires the commit that raises it to name the new number and the reason in the row's history (a raise is never silent - the growth is the event the gate exists to name).
law.ratchet_law: A budget may be lowered any time; the history records the lower value; a measured value below the budget never fails - it prints the headroom, and the ratchet (lowering the pin to the measured number) is the encouraged follow-up.
law.completeness_law: Every program the estate loads carries a row in BOTH envelopes. A loaded program missing from the ledger fails the battery on every run, census mode included - the inventory gate arms at landing and is never deferred; only the budget comparison defers.
law.census_law: A null budget is census debt, named honestly: the battery measures the program, prints the number into the run log (MASS-CENSUS rows), and the budget comparison stays deferred while armed is false. The arming commit pins the measured numbers from a watched CI run and flips armed to true in the same change - no half-armed state exists (armed true with any null budget is an invalid ledger).
